title: Next.js skill lookup used a stale plugin cache root
description: The initial skill-read command targeted an incorrect plugin root. The pattern recurred when relevant Next.js references were resolved beside SKILL.md even though this installed package stores them under a references subdirectory.
root_cause: The skill-root alias from the current catalog was not expanded before constructing the filesystem path.
solution: Resolved the current catalog path, listed the installed skill package with rg --files, and read the required references from its actual references subdirectory.

strategies: Expand the current skill-root alias before every skill read
Do not infer plugin cache ownership from similarly named runtime directories
code_patterns: Avoid: hand-constructing a cached plugin path
Use: the exact root mapping supplied in the available-skills catalog

title: Exploratory package probe requested unpublished server versions
description: A compatibility check guessed that @y/websocket-server versions 0.1.3 and 0.1.4 might exist instead of listing published versions first.

context.code_snippet: npm view @y/websocket-server@0.1.3 dependencies; npm view @y/websocket-server@0.1.4 dependencies

error_message: npm error E404 No match found for version 0.1.3; npm error E404 No match found for version 0.1.4
root_cause: Version-specific metadata was queried before discovering the package's published version list.
solution: Listed published versions, ran the required protocol test, and replaced the incompatible server package with the Yjs 13-compatible server bundled by y-websocket 2.1.0.

strategies: Run npm view <package> versions before querying historical metadata
Prefer integration verification over assumptions about protocol compatibility
code_patterns: Avoid: npm view package@guessed-version
Use: npm view package versions --json before selecting a version
tests_to_add: Run two-client Yjs synchronization against the selected server version

title: Selected WebSocket server used an incompatible Yjs major
description: The initial dependency set combined Tiptap's stable Yjs 13 collaboration stack with @y/websocket-server 0.1.5, which depends on a Yjs 14 prerelease. Both test clients reported initial sync, but document updates did not replicate.
error_message: Timed out while replicating an edit between two clients.
root_cause: Package-name compatibility was assumed before comparing the transitive Yjs major used by the server with Tiptap's required Yjs major.
solution: Removed @y/websocket-server, installed y-websocket 2.1.0 whose bundled server shares the root Yjs 13 dependency, and reran the two-client test successfully.

strategies: Inspect peer and transitive major versions before selecting collaboration transports
Require a real update-propagation test, not only successful connection and sync flags
code_patterns: Avoid: mixing a Yjs 14 server with a Yjs 13 editor stack
Use: npm ls yjs y-websocket --depth=1 and a two-client replication check
tests_to_add: Keep npm run verify:yjs in the required verification suite

title: Selected ESLint latest before checking plugin peer ranges
description: The first toolchain manifest used ESLint 10.7.0 even though the Next.js lint plugin chain did not yet declare compatibility with ESLint 10.
error_message: npm ls reported invalid ESLint peer dependencies.
root_cause: The registry's latest version was selected before checking the supported peer range of the installed framework lint plugins.
solution: Pinned ESLint 9.39.5, reinstalled dependencies, and verified npm run lint with zero errors.

strategies: Check framework-plugin peer dependency ranges before selecting a linter major
Treat npm ls invalid output as a blocking compatibility signal
code_patterns: Avoid: pairing each package's independent latest major
Use: a mutually compatible framework toolchain matrix
tests_to_add: Run npm ls and npm run lint after dependency installation

title: Passed a dotenv example directly to Prettier without a parser
description: The documentation-format command included .env.example in an explicit Prettier file list even though Prettier does not infer a parser for dotenv files.
error_message: No parser could be inferred for file .env.example.
root_cause: An unknown file type was included without --ignore-unknown or an explicit supported parser.
solution: Left the already-canonical dotenv file unchanged and scoped format:check to supported source, configuration, script, and README file types.

strategies: Do not pass dotenv files to Prettier without a dedicated plugin
Keep formatting scripts scoped to file types supported by the installed formatter
code_patterns: Avoid: prettier .env.example
Use: explicit supported globs or --ignore-unknown
tests_to_add: Run npm run format:check in the final verification suite

title: Direct Supabase changelog Markdown URL was rejected
description: The required changelog fetch attempted to open https://supabase.com/changelog.md directly, but the web safety layer rejected that URL form.
error_message: URL https://supabase.com/changelog.md is not safe to open (non-retryable error).
root_cause: The documentation fetch used a direct Markdown route unsupported by the active web safety layer.
solution: Switched to official Supabase changelog search results and opened the relevant SSR/auth changelog entry from the supported canonical page.

strategies: Use official-domain search when a documentation Markdown route is rejected as non-retryable
Do not retry the same blocked URL form
code_patterns: Avoid: repeated direct open of a rejected .md route
Use: domain-restricted search followed by canonical page open

title: Combined Supabase documentation query exceeded connector complexity
description: One GraphQL documentation request combined auth, RLS, and migration searches with nested subsection content and exceeded the connector's complexity limit.

context.code_snippet: auth + rls + migrations aliases with nested subsections in one query

error_message: Supabase Content API GraphQL error: query exceeds complexity limit.
root_cause: The query optimized for one round trip instead of the connector's bounded GraphQL complexity.
solution: Split discovery into focused searches with limited result counts and shallower fields, then used official pages for the relevant details.

strategies: Issue one focused Supabase documentation topic per search query
Request subsections only after identifying a relevant guide
code_patterns: Avoid: multi-topic aliased searches with full nested content
Use: small searchDocs queries with title, href, and bounded content

title: Type check ran between producer and consumer prop updates
description: The protected room page began passing authenticated identity and initial version metadata before CollaborativeRoom had been updated to declare and consume those props.
error_message: Property 'currentUser' does not exist on type 'CollaborativeRoomProps'.
root_cause: An intentionally incremental type check was run after the server-side interface producer changed but before the client-side consumer was wired.
solution: Update CollaborativeRoom and its version-history rail to accept the new serializable props, then rerun type checking after the integration boundary is complete.

strategies: When a prop contract spans a Server and Client Component, patch both sides in the same integration batch
Treat interim type checks as diagnostics and rerun after the complete interface change
code_patterns: Avoid: changing only the JSX caller before a compile checkpoint
Use: update the caller and CollaborativeRoomProps together
tests_to_add: Keep npm run typecheck after the history UI is connected

title: Truthy error check did not discriminate nullable action data
description: Version-history UI branches checked a nullable string error by truthiness, which did not prove to TypeScript that the paired data field was non-null.
root_cause: The result union used correlated nullable fields rather than a literal status discriminator, and truthiness allowed an empty string case in TypeScript's control-flow model.
solution: Guard on result.data === null so the remaining branch has a non-null success payload.

strategies: Narrow correlated action-result unions using an exact null check
Prefer a literal ok discriminator for more complex result contracts
code_patterns: Avoid: if (result.error) followed by result.data access
Use: if (result.data === null) return; then access result.data
tests_to_add: Keep strict TypeScript checking for client/server action boundaries

title: Connection effect synchronously reset React state
description: The first authenticated connection implementation reset several display states directly in the effect body before synchronizing with fetch and WebSocket systems.
error_message: react-hooks/set-state-in-effect: Calling setState synchronously within an effect can trigger cascading renders.
root_cause: Retry-display initialization was placed in the external-system effect instead of the user event that changes the retry attempt.
solution: Moved retry resets into the reconnect callback and keyed the room client component so navigation initializes a fresh state boundary.

strategies: Initialize state in useState and reset it in the event that changes an effect dependency
Keep effect bodies focused on subscriptions and asynchronous external synchronization
code_patterns: Avoid: synchronous setState calls at the top of a connection effect
Use: reset in reconnect handler, then increment connectionAttempt
tests_to_add: Keep React hook lint rules enabled

title: Generated apply_patch additions omitted line prefixes
description: A dynamically assembled audit-log patch prefixed only the first generated entry with a plus sign, so apply_patch rejected the remaining lines as invalid hunk syntax.
error_message: apply_patch verification failed: invalid hunk; Expected update hunk to start with a @@ context marker
root_cause: The generated array entries were joined without mapping each physical patch line to an addition line beginning with +.
solution: Mapped every generated log entry to a plus-prefixed line before joining and reapplied the audit patch successfully.

strategies: Prefix every dynamically generated addition line before composing an apply_patch hunk
Keep generated patches small and anchored to exact tail context
code_patterns: Avoid: entries.join("\n")
Use: entries.map((entry) => `+${entry}`).join("\n")

title: Profile integration changes missed repository formatting
description: The first formatting gate found two newly edited files whose multiline expressions did not match the repository's Prettier output.

context.code_snippet: Hand-formatted multiline validation and Supabase query expressions

error_message: Code style issues found in 2 files. Run Prettier with --write to fix.
root_cause: The edited multiline TypeScript and JavaScript expressions were not formatted before running the formatting gate.
solution: Ran the pinned Prettier version on the two reported files and scheduled the formatting check to run again.

strategies: Format touched source and verification files before the full static-check batch
Use the repository-pinned formatter instead of manually predicting line wrapping
code_patterns: Avoid: relying on manual wrapping for nested conditions
Use: npx prettier --write on the exact touched files
tests_to_add: Keep npm run format:check in the required verification gate

title: Index timestamp parser ignored trailing JSON punctuation
description: A helper script tried to extract the mistake-index timestamp with a regular expression that required a quote at end of line, but the JSON property correctly ended with a comma.
root_cause: The parser assumed the captured JSON string was the final token on the line and did not account for the required trailing comma.
solution: Read the existing property directly and applied an exact-context patch without parsing it through a fragile end-of-line expression.

strategies: Use exact JSON property context for small apply_patch updates
When parsing JSON, parse the document structurally instead of matching punctuation with a regular expression
code_patterns: Avoid: regexes that assume JSON property punctuation
Use: exact apply_patch context or JSON.parse for read-only extraction

title: Initial offline verifier mixed CJS execution with browser and Node type assumptions
description: The first TypeScript offline verifier used top-level await under the repository's CommonJS package mode, typed an ignored stdin child as fully piped, retained possibly undefined environment values across closures, and passed the ws constructor where y-websocket declared the DOM WebSocket shape.

context.code_snippet: top-level await; ChildProcessWithoutNullStreams with ignored stdin; WebSocketPolyfill: WebSocket

error_message: TS2322/TS2345 type errors and tsx: Top-level await is currently not supported with the cjs output format.
root_cause: The new verifier copied runtime patterns from untyped ESM scripts without adapting them to strict TypeScript and the package's CommonJS module classification.
solution: Wrapped execution in an async main function, piped all child streams, validated environment values through a string-returning helper, guarded indexed array access, and explicitly bridged the ws constructor to y-websocket's browser-facing option type.

strategies: Match test bootstrap style to the repository module mode before the first run
Run strict typecheck alongside every new TypeScript integration verifier
code_patterns: Avoid: top-level await in a CommonJS-classified TypeScript script
Use: async main().catch(...) with explicit Node/browser type boundaries
tests_to_add: Keep npm run typecheck and verify:offline-sync in the same feature gate

title: Mutable WebSocket provider was reachable through React state
description: The first local-first refactor stored the WebsocketProvider inside a useState connection object and later updated its params and connection state during token refresh.
error_message: react-hooks/immutability: Modifying a value returned from useState(), which should not be modified directly.
root_cause: A mutable external-system object was grouped with render state for convenience, making legitimate provider mutations look like direct React state mutation.
solution: Kept mutable provider operations behind a ref and exposed the same stable provider as a read-only render handle in the connection state.

strategies: Store mutable external clients in refs and expose only immutable render data through state
Run React hook lint immediately after connection lifecycle refactors
code_patterns: Avoid: state.provider.params = value
Use: providerRef.current.params = value for mutations and a stable state handle for child props
tests_to_add: Keep react-hooks/immutability enabled in the required lint gate

title: Provider ref was read during React render
description: The first fix for mutable provider state moved the WebsocketProvider entirely to a ref, but then read providerRef.current while deciding whether to render the editor and while passing its provider prop.
error_message: react-hooks/refs: Cannot access refs during render.
root_cause: The ref-only design satisfied the immutability rule for mutations but violated the React compiler rule that refs are not render data and do not trigger updates.
solution: Stored the same stable provider as an immutable handle in the initialized connection state for rendering while retaining the ref as the only path used for mutable lifecycle operations.

strategies: Separate the render handle for an external client from the ref used to mutate its lifecycle
Treat refs as effect and event-handler storage, never as render conditions or JSX props
code_patterns: Avoid: provider={providerRef.current}
Use: provider={connection.provider} while lifecycle effects mutate providerRef.current
tests_to_add: Keep react-hooks/refs enabled in the required lint gate

title: Room settings JSX was returned inside a data-fetch try block
description: The owner settings Server Component returned its JSX from the same try block used to classify repository access errors, which React lint rejects because render errors are not caught by that try/catch.

context.code_snippet: try { const room = await getRoomSettings(...); return <RoomSettingsPanel room={room} />; }

error_message: react-hooks/error-boundaries: Avoid constructing JSX within try/catch
root_cause: Data-access error classification and component construction were kept in one lexical block instead of ending the try after the awaited read.
solution: Store the fetched settings in a variable inside the try/catch and return JSX only after the catch block.

strategies: Limit Server Component try blocks to awaited operations that are expected to throw
Construct JSX after access-error classification
code_patterns: Avoid: return <Component /> inside data-fetch try
Use: let data; try { data = await read(); } catch { ... } return <Component data={data} />

title: Room wiring left retired imports and action contract parameters unused
description: The first focused lint pass found retired placeholder-control icons, an unused room-name prop, and required useActionState contract parameters that the current ESLint configuration does not exempt by underscore prefix.
error_message: @typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars warnings for retired imports, roomName, and Server Action parameters
root_cause: Placeholder controls were removed without pruning all imports, and action signatures retained unnamed contract inputs without explicitly consuming them.
solution: Remove retired imports, render the real room name, and explicitly consume required action-state/form arguments with void expressions.

strategies: Prune imports in the same patch that replaces placeholder controls
Explicitly consume framework-required callback parameters under strict unused-variable rules
code_patterns: Avoid: relying on underscore prefixes when ESLint is not configured to ignore them
Use: void state; void formData for required-but-unused callback inputs
tests_to_add: Run focused ESLint immediately after UI contract wiring

title: New room verifier scripts failed their first formatting preflight
description: Prettier check reported the newly created room-management verifier and the adapted version-history verifier needed mechanical formatting before execution.
error_message: Code style issues found in 2 files. Run Prettier with --write to fix.
root_cause: The large verifier patch was checked before the repository formatter had been applied to the new JavaScript structure.
solution: Applied Prettier to both verifier files before running functional verification.

strategies: Format newly created verifier scripts before the first formatting gate
code_patterns: Avoid: expecting a large generated script patch to already match mechanical wrapping
Use: prettier --write followed by prettier --check
